patients.label: 79-year-old man with perioral angioedema in the post-anesthesia care unit after transurethral resection of bladder under general anesthesia

identity_evidence.quote: a 79‑year-old male patient undergoing transurethral resection of a bladder tumor

attribution_limitations: Preoperative assessment did not reveal any personal or family history of angioedema; subsequently the patient revealed a history of HAE. This is read as a sequence of disclosure, not a source conflict. The HAE is also called previously unrecognized and unknown, while the diagnostic hypothesis was already supported by the patient's pre-existing clinical documentation.
The edema is called acute facial edema in the abstract and perioral edema involving both upper and lower lips in the case text.
Laryngeal mask airway insertion is called the trigger in the case description but only a likely trigger or sufficient to precipitate edema in the discussion.
The patient was on angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor therapy; the discussion mentions ACEi-related angioedema only as literature.
The case text says the patient "was scheduled for" transurethral resection; the abstract and procedure duration indicate it was performed.
The sentence about the next two hours does not name its anchor, and the later "within two hours" statement is also unanchored.
The C1-Inhibitor result is described only as below the normal range; the type of HAE, a numeric level and whether quantitative or functional are not stated.
General anesthesia was chosen given technical difficulties for spinal anesthesia; the source does not say whether a spinal block was attempted.

claims.text: A 79-year-old man with a history of hypertension on angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor therapy and type II diabetes mellitus (ASA 2) was scheduled for transurethral resection of bladder. Preoperative assessment did not reveal a personal or family history of angioedema, and there were no previous anesthetic complications. Because of technical difficulties for spinal anesthesia, general anesthesia was used with a size 4 I-gel laryngeal mask airway, and the procedure lasted about 60 minutes.

He then revealed a history of hereditary angioedema, was transferred to the intensive care unit for close observation and received subcutaneous icatibant 30 mg.
